plan: My private value is $30. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. If I bid less, I risk losing the item even when winning would be profitable. If I bid more, I might pay more than the item is worth to me. Since this is a single round with no repeated interactions, bidding exactly $30 maximizes my expected profit by ensuring I win only when the item is truly worth more than the second-highest bid.

My private value is $7. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid your true value. By bidding $7, I ensure:
1. If my value is below others' bids, I naturally lose
2. If I win, I'll pay less than my value
3. Bidding above $7 risks paying more than the item is worth to me
4. Bidding below $7 risks unnecessarily losing a potentially profitable item
So a direct, honest bid matching my private value seems most rational.

My private value is $36. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is to bid my true value. By bidding exactly $36, I maximize my potential profit:
- If others bid lower, I win and pay less than my value
- If others bid higher, I lose but wouldn't have made profit anyway
- Bidding above $36 risks paying more than the item is worth to me
- Bidding below $36 risks losing a potentially profitable auction
